points.description: States that the number of operations in the best case is N, the length of the array (linear in N).
points.partial_credit: Half marks for an approximate count such as 'linear time' or 'about n comparisons' without tying it to the array length.

points.description: States that the best-case scenario is when the array is already sorted.
points.partial_credit: Half marks for a vague description such as 'when the elements are in order' or 'when little work is needed' without saying the array is sorted.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both the count (N, the length of the array) and the scenario (the array is already sorted). Part marks go to a half-stated count or a vague description of the scenario, as listed above. A student who gives a wrong count, such as N squared, or names a different scenario such as a reverse-sorted array, loses that point's marks but keeps credit for the other point.
